Here is the road trip I just finished! Started and ended in Toronto, Ontario, Canada.

The little circles are where I stayed the night. You'll notice that there aren't any between Calgary, AB and Toronto. My cousin and I took turns driving and ended up doing the 36 hour drive non-stop (except for gas, food, and coffee).

I'd be happy to answer any questions about any of the places I went to!

You don´t really see a lot of little circles.

How long did it take?
I was gone for just under 6 weeks. Some of the circles are hard to see (I'm bad with sharpies apparently). There should be 18 or 19 circles. I will list them in another comment.

Places I slept (In order order of when I slept there)

  • Harvey Illinois (just outside of Chicago)

  • Omaha Nebraska

  • Denver Colorado

  • Moab Utah

  • Salt Lake City Utah

  • Reno Nevada

  • San Francisco California (spent several nights)

  • Morro Bay California

  • Los Angeles California (spent a few days)

  • Grand Canyon Arizona (camped 2 nights)

  • Cathedral Gorge Nevada

  • Walker Lake Nevada (it sucked, don't go)

  • Meeks Bay (Lake Tahoe) California (camped 3 nights)

  • Redwoods National/State Park California

  • Beverly Beach Oregon

  • Seattle Washington (stayed just under a week)

  • Vancouver BC (stayed several days)

  • Calgary AB

  • Toronto ON

How much was the trip?

What location would you say was the priciest? The cheapest?

All in I spent between $2000 and $3000 (Canadian dollars). I stayed for free with friends/family when I was in SF, LA, Seattle, Vancouver, and Calgary. I stayed in motels from Toronto to Reno. Although in Reno I stayed in a casino but the room was super cheap (because they want you to go to the casino and spend all your money there).

I drank a lot of expensive coffee in Seattle and San Francisco but if you're not into that sort of thing then they would both be a lot cheaper. Visiting Lake Tahoe is not cheap. The campsites at the Grand Canyon and Redwoods National/State Park are not cheap either but they're gorgeous and well maintained so it's hard to complain.

The cheapest place was when we camped at Walker Lake in Nevada, it was like $3 for the night but it also sucked. 0/5 would not recommend. Would not visit again.

Hope that answers your questions :)
